subject: multiple background color in one plot

messages.author: 94b44552b8aba108
messages.subject: multiple background color in one plot
parts:
I have a data looks like this 


x   y      z 

1   1.2   a
2   1.5   a
3   1.9   b
4   2.3   b
5   2.5   b


I use 

ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_line()  

to get a line chart and I would like to change the background color based on the factors of z,  in this case,  I would like to split the chart background into 2 pieces perpendicular to x axis:  (1,2) and (3, 4, 5) and apply distinct colors to the two rectangular areas. 


Is there a way to do this?   I searched online but haven't found a good answer to this and thus check here for experts.  Thanks bunch!

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: multiple background color in one plot
parts:
You could do something like this:

d <- data.frame(x=1:5,y=c(1.2,1.5,1.9,2.3,2.5),z=c("a","a","b","b","b"))
library(plyr)
d1 <- ddply(d,.(z),summarise,xmin=min(x)-.5,xmax=max(x)+.5) # data
for the background
ggplot(d)+geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y))+geom_rect(data=d1,aes(xmin=xmin,xmax=xmax,ymin=-Inf,ymax=Inf,fill=z),alpha=.2)

Ben
